source_text: Ἐπεὶ δὲ καὶ τὰ περὶ τοῦ καλουμένου ἀντιχρίστου παραῤῥιπτεῖ ὁ Κέλσος. ουτε τὰ ἐν τῷ Δανιὴλ οὔτε τὰ παρὰ τῷ Παύλῳ ἀναγνοὺς περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰρημένα οὔτε τὰ ἐν τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος προφητευθέντα περὶ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, ὀλίγα καὶ περὶ τούτου λεκτέον. ὅτι „ὥσπερ οὐχ ὅμοια πρόσωπα προσώποις. οὕτως οὐδὲ αἱ καρδίαι ὅμοιαι ταῖς καρδίαις τῶν ἀνθρώπων.“ δῆλον ὅτι εἶεν ἂν ἐν „ταῖς καρδίαις τῶν ἀνθρώπων“ διαφοραὶ καὶ τῶν πρὸς τὸ καλὸν νενευκότων, οὐκ ἐπ᾿ ἴσης καὶ παραπλησίως ἀλλήλοις πάντων τυπωθέντων καὶ μορφωθέντων πρὸς αὐτὸ, καὶ τῶν δι᾿ ἀμέλειαν τοῦ καλοῦ ἐπὶ τὰ ἐναντία ᾀττόντων· καὶ ἐν τούτοις γὰρ ἐν οἷς μέν ἐστι σφόδρα κεχυμένη ἡ κακία ἐν οἷς δ᾿ ἐπ᾿ ἔλαττον· τί οὖν ἄτοπον δύο, ἵν᾿ οὕτως ὀνομάσω, ἀκρότητας. τὴν μὲν τοῦ καλοῦ τὴν δὲ τοῦ ἐναντίου, ἐν ἀνθρώποις γίνεσθαι, ὥστε τὴν μὲν τοῦ καλοῦ ἀκρότητα εἶναι ἐν τῷ κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν νοουμένῳ ἀνθρώπῳ, ἀφ᾿ ου ἡ τοσαύτη ἔῤῥευσε τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπιστροφὴ καὶ θεραπεία καὶ βελτίωσις, τὴν δὲ τοῦ ἐναντίου ἐν τῷ κατὰ τὸν ὀνομαζόμενον ἀντίχριστον; πάντα δὲ τῇ ἑαυτοῦ προγνώσει ἐκπεριλαβὼν ὁ θεὸς καὶ ἰδὼν τὰ περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τούτων ἐβουλήθη περὶ τούτων γνωρίσαι διὰ τῶν προφητῶν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, ἵνα οἱ συνιέντες τῶν λόγων αὐτῶν οἰκειωθῶσι μὲν τῷ κρείττονι. φυλάξωνται δὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐναντίου. ἐχρῆν δὲ τὸν μὲν ἕτερον τῶν ἄκρων καὶ βέλτιστον υἱὸν ἀναγορεύεσθαι τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν ὑπεροχὴν, τὸν δὲ τούτῳ κατὰ διάμετρον ἐναντίον υἱὸν τοῦ πονηροῦ δαίμονος καὶ Σατανᾶ καὶ διαβόλου. εἶτ᾿ ἐπεὶ τότε μάλιστα τὸ φαῦλον ἐν τῇ χύσει τῆς κακίας καὶ τῇ ἀκρότητι αὐτῆς εἶναι χαρακτηρίζεται, ὅτε ὑποκρίνεται τὸ κρεῖττον, διὰ τοῦτο περὶ τὸν χείρονα γίνεται ἐκ συνεργίας τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ διαβόλου σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα καὶ δυνάμεις ψεύδους. ὑπὲρ γὰρ τὰς εἰς τοὺς γόητας γινομένας ἀπὸ δαιμόνων συνεργίας πρὸς τὰ φαυλότατα τῶν ἀνθρώπους ἀπατώντων γίνεται συνεργία ἀπ᾿ αὐτοῦ τοῦ διαβόλου ἐπὶ ἀπάτῃ τοῦ γένους τῶν ἀνθρώπων. Λέγει δὲ ὁ Παῦλος περὶ τούτου τοῦ καλουμένου ἀντιχρίστου διδάσκων καὶ παριστὰς μετά τινος ἐπικρύψεως, τίνα τρόπον ἐπιδημήσει καὶ πότε τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ διὰ τί· καὶ ὅρα εἰ μὴ σεμνότατα περὶ τούτων ὁ Παῦλος ἐκτίθεται καὶ οὐκ ἀξίως χλεύης τινὸς κἂν ἐλαχίστης·
pass_a_gloss: Since also Celsus has overlooked the things concerning the so-called antichrist, having not read what was said about him by Daniel or by Paul or what was prophesied by the Savior in the Gospels concerning his presence, it is necessary to speak briefly about this. That 'just as faces are not like faces, so also hearts are not like the hearts of men' is clear, for there would be differences in the hearts of men, both of those who have turned towards the good and of those who have turned towards the opposite things through neglect of the good; and among these, in some the evil is very much poured out, in others to a lesser degree; what then is absurd about there being two, as I might call them, extremes, one of the good and one of the opposite, occurring in men? So that the extreme of the good is in the man conceived according to Jesus, from whom such a great conversion and healing and improvement of the human race has occurred, and the extreme of the opposite is in the one called antichrist? But God, having foreknown all things and having seen the things concerning both of these, wished to make them known to men through the prophets, so that those understanding their words might become familiar with the better and guard against the opposite. It was necessary for the one who is the other extreme and the best to be proclaimed the Son of God because of his superiority, and the one who is opposite to him, the son of the evil demon and Satan and devil. And since then, especially when the worse is characterized by the outpouring of evil and its extreme, when it pretends to be the better, for this reason signs and wonders and powers of falsehood occur concerning the worse one through the cooperation of his father, the devil. For a cooperation from the devil himself occurs, beyond the cooperations from demons that occur towards the most worthless of men, deceiving them. Paul says concerning this so-called antichrist, teaching and presenting with a certain concealment, what kind of way he will make his appearance and when to the human race and why; and see if Paul does not discuss these things in a most dignified manner and not in a way worthy of any slight contempt;

choices.why: to convey the idea of two opposing ends of a spectrum
to convey the idea of something that is directly opposed to something else

pass_b_english: Since Celsus dismisses what is said about the so-called antichrist, having read neither Daniel nor Paul nor the Savior's own prophecies in the Gospels about his coming, a brief word on the subject is needed. As the proverb goes, "Just as faces are not alike, so also hearts are not like the hearts of men" (Prov 24:16 LXX). Clearly, then, there are differences among human hearts—some turned toward the good, others toward its opposite through neglect of the good—and among the latter, evil is poured out to a greater degree in some, to a lesser degree in others. So what is so absurd about the existence of two extremes in humanity, as I might call them: one of the good, the other of its opposite? The extreme of the good is found in the man conceived according to Jesus, from whom so great a turning, healing, and betterment of the human race has flowed; the extreme of the opposite resides in the one called antichrist. God, foreknowing all things and seeing the destinies of both, chose to make them known through the prophets, so that those who understand their words might attach themselves to the better and guard against the opposite (2 Thessalonians 2:3-4). It was fitting that the one extreme—the best—be proclaimed Son of God because of his excellence, and the other, diametrically opposed to him, be the son of the evil demon, Satan, and the devil. And precisely because evil is most intensely characterized by its outpouring and extremity when it counterfeits the better, signs and wonders and false powers accompany the worse one through the cooperation of his father, the devil. For a cooperation from the devil himself arises—beyond the demonic cooperations that deceive the most worthless of men—in order to deceive the human race. Paul speaks of this so-called antichrist, teaching and setting forth the matter with a certain reserve: how he will appear, when he will come to humankind, and why. And one must ask whether Paul does not treat these things with the utmost dignity, in no way deserving even the slightest contempt.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent version that correctly identifies the implied scriptural contexts (Proverbs 24:16 and 2 Thessalonians 2:3-4) without introducing errors. The distinction between the 'cooperation of the devil' and the 'cooperation of demons' is preserved. The translation of 'ἐπικρύψεως' as 'concealment' (Pass A) and 'reserve' (Pass B) is appropriate for the context of Paul's teaching style.
